newsitem.title: FRANCE: Press watchdog sends representative to Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Press watchdog sends representative to Hong Kong.

text.p: A Paris-based media watchdog said on Wednesday it had appointed a "correspondent" to Hong Kong to watch out for any violations of press freedom once the territory reverts to Chinese hands.
"Apparently the Chinese want to bring the Hong Kong media into line," Reporters sans Frontieres (Reporters without Borders) said in a statement.
"The new RSF correspondent in Hong Kong will be responsible for alerting the organisation to any infringements of press freedom there."
The group said its representative will be Sarah Poon, senior staff editor of the Reader's Digest Asia.
It said its decision to place a representative in Hong Kong had been taken in close cooperation with the Hong Kong Journalists' Association.
"The Beijing authorities' attitude towards Hong Kong's independent press will be a test of their willingness to respect human rights and freedoms in the former British colony," it said.
Britain is due to hand back sovereignty over Hong Kong to China at midnight on June 30.
